answer.rationale: Competitive pressure on price-sensitive SMB segment requires direct response. Memory_73 confirms targeted promotional pricing drives acquisition and revenue lift in SMB. However, risk exists: aggressive pricing may anchor expectations downward, harm long-term unit economics, or train customers to wait for discounts. This is not the theoretically optimal long-term play (enterprise_sales_assist per memory_44 would build higher-value pipeline), but the immediate threat of doubled churn makes inaction more dangerous than measured intervention. Standard experiment (not broad rollout) on promotional pricing preserves optionality—test with subset, monitor 30-day retention carefully (memory_31 showed -1% in signup simplification, warning that activation levers can trade off retention), and maintain parallel enterprise motion. If pricing test shows retention holds above -2%, scale; if worse, pivot to pairing promotional pricing with activation_messaging (memory_91 showed +1% retention lift) to improve stickiness of discounted cohorts.
